question: Does adult literacy move with GDP growth in a within-country panel where the schooling-years proxy does not?
estimand: standardized beta of adult literacy, S2 (country+year FE, 1995-2024 annual)
threshold: S2: literacy > 0 with CI excluding 0 AND (MYS_proxy CI includes 0 OR |std MYS| < 0.5*|std literacy|)
label: observed
note: S2 literacy CI includes 0 but S3 (5-year blocks) literacy is significant -> not a stable within-country association. standardized (pooled SD) betas in S2: literacy=0.4471 CI[-0.4256,1.3197], MYS_proxy=0.8706 CI[-1.5017,3.2428] (DERIVED: MYS_proxy = 6 + 6*(SE.SEC.CUAT.LO.ZS/100) + 3*(SE.SEC.CUAT.UP.ZS/100) + 4*(SE.TER.CUAT.BA.ZS/100)); S3 literacy=1.5200 CI[0.5397,2.5003] n=62; S1 literacy=0.2730; S4 DATA LIMITED (n=5 countries, only 4 have both periods); descriptive, not causal

question: Does economic complexity (ECI) move with growth in the same panel?
estimand: standardized beta of ECI, S2 (annual) with S3 cross-check
threshold: ECI > 0 with CI excluding 0 in BOTH S2 and S3; falsifier: CI includes 0 in both, or sign flip S2 vs S3
label: observed
note: ECI is not positive-significant in S2 or S3, so the frozen threshold (positive with CI excluding 0 in BOTH) fails; its S3 coefficient is significantly NEGATIVE. S2 ECI=-0.5813 CI[-1.6316,0.4689] n=127 G=23; S3 ECI=-2.5891 CI[-4.1116,-1.0665] n=62 G=25; S1 ECI=-0.0254; the ECI specification includes MYS_proxy (derived) as a control

question: Is the education-growth association steeper in more complex economies?
estimand: high-ECI minus low-ECI literacy slope (raw growth pp per literacy pp), S6
threshold: high-tercile literacy slope > low-tercile by >= 50% of the low magnitude, same sign, and bootstrap CI for the difference excluding 0
label: derived
note: high and low tercile slopes do not share a sign. literacy slopes (raw): low=0.0220, mid=0.3696, high=-0.0144; high-low=-0.0365 bootstrap 95% CI [-0.6468,1.6417] (B=1000, valid=992); relative difference=-1.65x the low slope; tercile n={'low': 43, 'mid': 42, 'high': 42}, countries={'low': 18, 'mid': 17, 'high': 18}; terciles formed on within-country-demeaned ECI; descriptive, no causal and no Africa reading

question: What actually moves together within countries?
estimand: largest |within-country r| among pairs with |r|>=0.4 and permutation p<0.05
threshold: no threshold (descriptive); 'stable' = |r|>=0.4, permutation p<0.05, sign stable across adult/youth literacy and across the two levels tested
label: derived
note: 45 of 45 pairs have n>=20; 17 reach |r|>=0.4 with permutation p<0.05; 17 also pass the sign-stability checks. Top |r| pairs (n>=20, p<0.05): cuat_up~MYS r=0.920 (n=193, p=0.0010, stable); lit~lit_youth r=0.909 (n=274, p=0.0010, stable); cuat_ba~MYS r=0.830 (n=193, p=0.0010, stable); cuat_up~cuat_ba r=0.684 (n=207, p=0.0010, stable); lsec_cmpt~urban r=0.674 (n=516, p=0.0010, stable). The S8 matrix contains MYS_proxy (derived). Nothing here is a direction claim
